result.topic_en: Euler squares the algebraic integral $\sqrt X+\sqrt Y=\sqrt{\Delta+2B(x+y)+C(x+y)^2}$ of $dx/\sqrt X = dy/\sqrt Y$ (with X, Y quadratic) to clear it of irrationality, then identifies its coefficients with his earlier canonical form $\alpha+2\beta(x+y)+\gamma(xx+yy)+2\delta xy=0$.
result.transcription:
) 33 (
Cum igitur ſit $\frac{dp}{dt}=\sqrt{X}+\sqrt{Y}$, aequatio integralis, quam ſumus adepti, erit
$\sqrt{X}+\sqrt{Y}=\sqrt{(\Delta+2B(x+y)+C(x+y)^2)}$,
quae adeo eſt algebraica; vbi notetur eſſe
$X=A+Bx+Cxx$ et $Y=A+By+Cyy$.

§. 29. Sumamus igitur quadrata, et noſtra aequatio integralis erit
$2A+B(x+y)+C(x^2+y^2)+2\sqrt{XY}$
$=\Delta+2B(x+y)+C(x+y)^2$, ſiue
$2A-B(x+y)-2Cxy+2\sqrt{XY}=\Delta$,
quae penitus ab irrationalitate liberata, poſito $\Delta-2A=\Gamma$ praebebit
$4XY=4AA+4AB(x+y)+4AC(xx+yy)$
$+4BBxy+4BCxy(x+y)+4CCxxyy$
$=\Gamma^2+2\Gamma B(x+y)+4\Gamma Cxy+BB(x+y)^2$
$+4BCxy(x+y)+4CCxxyy$
ſiue
$(4AA-\Gamma^2)+2B(2A-\Gamma)(x+y)+4(BB-\Gamma C)xy$
$+4AC(xx+yy)-B^2(x+y)^2=0$.

§. 30. Quod ſi iam hanc aequationem rationalem cum formula *canonica*, qua olim ſum vſus ad huiusmodi integrationes expediendas, comparemus, quae erat
$\alpha+2\beta(x+y)+\gamma(xx+yy)+2\delta xy=0$,
dum ſcilicet loco $(x+y)^2$ ſcribamus $(xx+yy)+2xy$, reperiemus fore
$\alpha=4AA-\Gamma^2$; $\beta=B(2A-\Gamma)$; $\gamma=4AC-B^2$;
$\delta=BB-2\Gamma C$.
Acta Acad Imp. Sc. Tom. II. P. I. E §. 31.

quae adeo eſt algebraica
items.english: The integral equation which we have obtained will be $\sqrt X+\sqrt Y=\sqrt{\Delta+2B(x+y)+C(x+y)^2}$, which is therefore algebraic.
Let us therefore take the squares, so as to free the integral equation from irrationality.

items.quote: Quod ſi iam hanc aequationem rationalem cum formula *canonica*, qua olim ſum vſus ad huiusmodi integrationes expediendas, comparemus
items.english: If we now compare this rational equation with the canonical formula which I formerly used to carry out integrations of this kind, we find the values of its coefficients.
